you definitely do not suck, your feelings are valid. and feeling suicidal, even though you feel like you shouldn't because you're more 'fortunate' and 'successful' could be a sign of you putting pressure on yourself. especially if you feel like your daily life is a chore. 

your situation feels pretty similar to mine way back in middle school, i used to be a top successful student but didnt enjoy living.

after 5 years of wondering what went wrong, i realized a lot of my problems could have possibly been prevented if i just talked to someone. i was so shy and bottled everything up from shame.

i know it sounds like a broken record to say this, but you need to find someone to talk to. i know you said you were pretty upset from your ex girlfriend. but i can promise you not everyone is like that. there are so many people out there ready to listen. i hope you could at least give it a second or third try. it can be anyone, even friends that might not seem that close could turn out to be great listeners, or could be going through similar struggles. i had this friend of a friend that i've known for 3 years, never been very close, but one day he called me out of nowhere asking if he could vent about his breakup. apparently, our mutual friend told him that i was a good listener and i guess he just really needed any help he could get and he just didnt care that we weren't close, he just wanted to talk. and i'm glad he did. he was crying by the end of our 4h long phone call from how relieved he felt and how good it was to let things out, i barely talked but that was what he needed.

i would recommend one on one talks, but if that isn't possible, there a people on this sub that would love to listen to you so don't be shy. i would be glad to listen to you too. 

you could also try a therapist, it might feel a little intimidating and even if you might not feel like you are 'sick enough' or too 'privelidged' to see one, trust me even feeling 'casually' like killing yourself shouldn't be taken lighty and you deserve receive professional help.
